Looping in procurement sequencing detail — keeping it tight so the pilot is not blocked:

1) DPA: priority #1. Novamed legal provides redlines by 07/14 -> Redwood legal will incorporate and return consolidated redlines same day -> target execution 07/16 via DocuSign. (DPA must be in place before PII transfer.)
2) Order form: commercial terms can be agreed in parallel. We recommend: final commercial worksheet (price/seat/term) locked by 07/16 -> Redwood to issue final order form 07/16 -> submit to Novamed finance for approval. Typical finance SLA is 3 business days (so target countersign 07/21).
3) MSA: if a full MSA amendment is required we can push a limited-scope addendum that covers pilot scope and liability caps, to avoid delaying the pilot. If Novamed requires broader MSA changes, that will be tracked as a dependent activity but should not block the pilot if we have the DPA and a pilot addendum.

Gate definitions for production-onboard (Marissa to define acceptance):
- Connectivity and API stability (99.5% p99 response under test load)
- Data integrity checks for PII handling (checksum and audit log pass)
- Model output sanity (support false-positive threshold <5% on labeled sample)
- Security review sign-off (IAM and network configs)

I will also add an item for billing: if order form contains advance commitment, finance needs billing contact and PO number before countersign.

Karthik
Director, Commercial Ops | Redwood Inference
